A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the canonical change-of-variable method provides a simple, diagrammatic and manifestly unitary way of obtaining the full set of tree and one-loop MHV amplitues, and their off-shell generalisations.
the MHV lagranian is not a new theory, but rather a new formulation of the original light-conge Yang-Mills theory.

the MHV lagrangean is a valid starting point for perturbative quantum field theory in D-dimensions, and in particular that the CSW rules are a valid method for computing tree-level amplitudes in any signature, as well as loop amplitudes with complex external momenta, provided that the MHV amplituhedron is used to compute the loop integrals.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the equivalence theorem evasion and the dimensional regularisation are not mutually exclusive, but rather they can be achieved simultaneously by the canonical change of field variables.

the MHV lagranigian and MHV rules are equivalent to light-cone Yang Mills and the usual Feynman rules, and that the canonical transformation that yields MHV rules also yields the extra contributions that are needed for the equivalence theorem to hold.
, in the presence of dimensional regularisation, the MHV lagragian is not a true off-shell lagrangian, but rather a re-organised form of light-cone Yang Mills, which is a valid off-shell lagrangain.
